_comment: New conversations of the HEMS missions (boarding, briefing, debriefing), written for the voice pack system. Each message has four options; option k of every line of a conversation belongs together (coherent variety). No wav exists yet: the LVAR numbers are reserved for the wav files to be recorded later. The mission calls them with the voice code APP (L:PLT{VCP}47).

messages.trigger: after the crew boarded and the comm check
o: Everybody aboard? Check your belts and doors.
All aboard. Belts, doors and bags, please check.
Crew, quick cabin check. Belts and doors.
Let's make sure we are all set. Belts and doors check.
Copilot, belts fastened and cockpit doors closed.
Copilot checked. My belt is on and the right door is closed.
Belts are on up front, doors closed on my side.
Front seats are secure, copilot ready.
{@PAX3} here. Medical kit secured and bags stowed.
Medical bag is strapped down, Doc ready.
Doc: the kit is on board and everything is stowed.
I have the medical equipment secured, Doc is set.
Rear crew ready. Hoist and stretcher are secured.
Cabin is clear, the hoist and the stretcher are fixed.
Chief here, the cabin is ready for flight.
Hoist gear and stretcher are checked, rear is ready.
Good. Let's start the checklist.
Perfect. Starting the checklist now.
Thank you all. Checklist time.
Copy, all set. We go on with the checklist.

messages.trigger: after the dispatcher read the dispatch
o: Dispatch received. Let's take this mission.
We have our dispatch. Quick briefing, everyone.
Crew, we got a dispatch. Short briefing.
Dispatch is in. We take it.
Copy. I will set the route and watch the weather.
Copilot copy. Navigation and radios are mine.
I take the route and the radio calls.
Understood. I set the route and monitor the traffic.
Doc copy. I will assess the patient as soon as we land.
Doc here. Patient assessment first, then we decide.
I take the patient on arrival, Doc ready.
Copy. I will start with the patient assessment.
Rear crew copy. Hoist and ground gear are ready.
Chief copy. Equipment for ground or hoist is on board.
Rear crew ready for hoist or ground operation.
We are set for whatever the site needs.
Good. We lift off when ready.
Thanks. Lift off as soon as the checklist is complete.
Very good. Let's go and help them.
Alright, let's bring everybody home safe.

messages.trigger: after the mission, landed at the base, patient outcome good
o: Good job, everyone. That went well.
Well done, crew. A clean mission.
Thank you all. Good teamwork out there.
That was a solid mission. Thanks, crew.
Smooth flight, {@PLT}. Nice work.
Copilot: no issues from the cockpit.
Good flying, {@PLT}. The routes were clean.
Everything on the instruments looked fine.
Doc: the patient is stable and handed over.
The patient was delivered in good condition.
Handover done, the patient is in good hands.
I am happy with the clinical outcome.
Rear crew: gear is stowed, nothing to report.
Hoist and equipment are clean and secured.
Chief here, the cabin is tidy and ready for the next one.
All equipment is back on board, no damage.
Thanks. Let's finish the shutdown.
Copy. Shutdown checklist now.
Great. Let's secure the helicopter.
Good. Now the shutdown, then a coffee.

messages.trigger: after the mission, landed at the base, patient outcome bad
o: That was a hard one, crew.
A tough mission. Thank you for staying focused.
We did all we could, crew.
Not the outcome we wanted, but we gave everything.
We did what we could, {@PLT}.
Nobody could have done more.
We followed every procedure, {@PLT}.
It was out of our hands in the end.
Doc: I will write the clinical report.
I will file the report and review the case.
I will document everything for the team.
The medical report is on me, we will go through it.
Thank you all. We talk about it later.
Take a moment, then we debrief at base.
Thanks, {@CPL}, thanks everyone. We will review it together.
Rest a bit. We talk when you are ready.
